factor_key.label: Game environment
factor_key.text: Vegas spread and over/under, turned into this team's implied points. Higher-scoring expected games mean more plays and more scoring chances. Baseline: a typical game for the position over the last two seasons.

factor_key.label: Opponent defense
factor_key.text: How this opponent's defense has played lately: fantasy points and targets allowed to this position, EPA per dropback allowed, yards per carry and per target allowed, and how many plays opponents run against them. Baseline: a league-typical defense.

factor_key.label: Opponent DB injuries
factor_key.text: Regular defensive backs (50%+ of snaps recently) on the opposing team who are ruled out or on IR. Baseline: a fully healthy secondary.

factor_key.label: Teammate absences
factor_key.text: Share of the team's recent targets and carries belonging to teammates who are out this week, which frees up opportunities. Baseline: nobody missing.

factor_key.label: QB vs. recent QB play
factor_key.text: This week's starting QB's longer-run efficiency (EPA per dropback, weighted toward recent games) compared with the QB play behind this player's recent stats. With a new starter, this is the upgrade or downgrade. With the same starter, it is the model expecting his recent form to drift back toward his longer track record. Baseline: the same quality of QB play as recent weeks.

factor_key.label: Weather
factor_key.text: Kickoff forecast for outdoor stadiums (wind and temperature). Domes and retractable roofs are neutral. Baseline: 65°F with 5 mph wind.

factor_key.label: Own injury status
factor_key.text: The player's own injury designation and practice participation this week. Baseline: healthy and practicing fully.

factor_key.label: Betting market
factor_key.text: Sportsbooks post lines for some players' receptions, yards and anytime TD. We turn each line into an expected stat and compare it with our model's own estimate of that stat. Where they disagree, we split the difference: half the gap is added to the projection. Where they agree, nothing changes. Unlike the factors above, this is the actual change made to the model's number, not a sensitivity.
